questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always loved the city and wanted to live here - and I have been learning the language for many years now as well, so that also played a part.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as I had an Erasmus meeting at the university quite early on and was put in contact with the relevant people.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An informative meeting, help getting a student card etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in the Cité Universitaire and would highly recommend it - especially the Fondation Danoise.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It really enriches your experience of the city to live in a non-touristy area, and the public transport is quite convenient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to look through the course catalogue on your own time and then personally contact the professors to ask for a spot in their class - and then register it with a third party.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a coordinator you could e-mail for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50/50 I would say, but I ended up with some really interesting classes - although it was a few weeks into the semester until everything was in place, so be patient and vigilant.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Send e-mails as early as possible to secure a spot in the courses you really want (especially during the spring semester, where some courses are already filled up from the previous semester) and be open to experience new courses if it doesn't work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied in difficulty but there was a lot of reading for each class and I had to take many classes to fulfill my ects-requirement for the semester, so it felt fitting for Master level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more oral presentations (a few in each course over the semester), but otherwise quite similar with class discussions and readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contemporary British Theatre, Littérature Américaine - corps et santé, Littérature Postcoloniale, The Long 1980s, Colours in Victorian Britain, and American Salt Water Writing.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend anything with Professors Juliette Utard, Thomas Constantinesco and Charlotte Ribeyrol.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Really good bread and cheese is so cheap (as well as books), but a good coffee in a café is quite expensive (around 5-7 euros).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really look into this, but there was a cool cinema club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Perhaps a local book or movie club to help learn the language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just take in the city - go for long walks, give yourself time to stop somewhere and sit for a bit (listen to a street musician or read a book), use the many museums and parks, stroll in le Marais etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy once I understood the social codes (saying hello when you enter a place etc).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students in my department were extremely nice and welcoming, so it luckily came quite easily - but otherwise just be brave and ask people for coffee.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmth of the people, the slower tempo and the appreciation for culture/humanities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared from home for the course registration process, try to learn the language (even if just on a café-level) and learn to just be on your own in the city as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a more analogue lifestyle (all my exams were in hand, pen on paper etc).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made some of the most meaningful friendships of my life here and really grew as a person.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To juggle the academic pressure with my social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
